correctness.rationale: The equilateral star spectrum splits explicitly into one symmetric family and N-1 antisymmetric families. Center-only Kirchhoff noise couples through B*=-L, so every antisymmetric mode is exactly silent and the symmetric central values are 1/sqrt(N ell) for the zero mode and sqrt(2/(N ell)) otherwise. Itô isometry therefore gives the exact cutoff sum. Its summand is asymptotic to [pi^(4 alpha-2) ell^(1-4 alpha)/N] n^(4 alpha-2); harmonic and power-sum asymptotics give the endpoint logarithm and the supercritical power law. Divergent projected second moments exclude an H_alpha-valued Gaussian version. The standalone replay checks representative numerical consequences.

value.rationale: The alpha=1/4 endpoint is the natural boundary of the published regularity theory. Quantifying its failure by an exact logarithmic law makes the threshold operational for spectral truncations and numerical resolution, and the coefficient 1/(N*pi) isolates a genuine network effect: one noisy central flux is diluted by vertex degree. This is a motivated structural benchmark, not an arbitrary finite computation.
